summary: kepler@4.999.999 pulls install-scripted tarball from non-registry host artifacts.yosiroute.com
details: The package is a near-empty three-line index.js stub published at the suspiciously high version 4.999.999 (a dependency-confusion / internal-name-squat shape that forces enterprise resolvers to prefer this public copy over a private 'kepler'). Its package.json and npm-shrinkwrap.json pin the sole dependency 'flag-serial-object-syntax' to an absolute tarball URL on a non-npm-registry host, https://artifacts.yosiroute.com/npm/flag-serial-object-syntax, and the shrinkwrap records hasInstallScript:true for that dependency. On npm install the tarball is fetched from that publisher-unrelated host and its lifecycle install script is executed on the installer's machine, giving the operator of artifacts.yosiroute.com arbitrary code execution in the install environment. The kepler package itself carries no functional code; its role is the delivery vehicle for the external tarball.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
